To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
EBV-associated malignances are treatable with T cell-based therapies.
T cells are a key component in the host immune response against EBV-associated malignances.
T cell therapy is an effective approach for the treatment of EBV-associated posttransplant lymphoproliferaive disease and other EBV-associated cancers.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and clinical evaluation of T cell-based therapies for the treatment of EBV-associated cancers.
the development of T cell-based therapies for the treatment and/or prophylaxis of EBV-associated disease.
the development of immunotherapy and prophylactic vaccine approaches to treat and prevent EBV-related diseases.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
T cells can be used to successfully treat EBV-associated malignances, and that T cell-based immunotherapies will play a key role in the future treatment of these diseases.

the development of T cell-based therapies for the treatment of EBV-associated lymphoproliferation has been a success story, and that the future of this approach is promising.
the EBV latent antigens are attractive therapeutic targets for EBV-associated tumours and the EBV lytic antigens are attractive prophylactic targets for EBV infection.

EBV is an important human pathogen and that it is associated with a wide variety of malignancies.
